title: Consumer Outcomes in Embedded Journeys
summary: How platform design, personalisation and frictionless journeys shape customer decisions, and how the firm tests and evidences fair outcomes, suitability and complaints handling when a partner owns the interface.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How platform design, personalisation and frictionless journeys shape customer decisions, and how the firm tests and evidences fair outcomes, suitability and complaints handling when a partner owns the interface.
Learning Objectives: Identify harms from choice architecture, dark patterns and frictionless credit
Apply disclosure, product governance and suitability in partner-owned journeys
Design outcome testing, complaints handling and redress across the chain
Syllabus: Choice architecture, defaults and dark patterns
Embedded credit, buy now, pay later and investment nudges
Personalised pricing, profiling and fair treatment
Complaints, redress and outcome monitoring across partners
Intended Audience: Founders, chief executives, product and partnerships leads at payment, e-money, investment and fintech firms
Compliance, MLRO, risk, outsourcing and third-party risk staff overseeing partners and distributors
Technology, data and API leads responsible for open finance connections and platform integrations
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of payments, e-money, investment distribution or fintech partnerships is helpful. No technical background in APIs is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FSB, Enhancing Cross-border Payments: Stage 3 Roadmap (2020)
